proof_spans.label: complete planar gadget construction, native figure, and two-case proof

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite planar range hypergraphs
standard_prerequisites.statement: A range captures exactly the input points lying in it. Bottomless rectangles have two vertical sides and a horizontal upper side, with no lower bound.
standard_prerequisites.use: Verify each explicitly chosen edge has exactly m points.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary counting and geometric separation
standard_prerequisites.use: Use strict coordinate inequalities to set rectangle boundaries between finite point coordinates, and use four disjoint triples among at least12 ordered points.

core_obligations: Build m separated anchored gadgets so the base points themselves form one m-point captured edge, forcing a selected anchor in one gadget.

Arrange the A, B and C families in opposite coordinate orders so each B_i and each C_i,j forms a captured m-edge, while a rectangle can also select all m-2 A-points and exactly one prescribed point from each of B and C.
If the chosen anchor has another selected A-point, force a captured m-edge with at least four selected points using a B-hit and a corresponding C-hit.
If the anchor is the only selected A-point, use the m-3 other A-points plus every consecutive B-triple to force at least four selected B-points, contradicting shallowness on B_i itself.

proof_roadmap.step: Place the base edge and the original three-family coordinate gadget, including the full native TikZ figure and precise inequalities.
With two selected A-points, choose selected b_i^j and c_i,j^l; the coordinate ordering gives exactly m-2+1+1 captured points, at least four selected.
Without another selected A-point, every three consecutive B-points must be hit; for m>=12 four disjoint triples force four hits in the m-edge B_i.

difficulty_reason: The numerical pigeonhole step is elementary, but the main task is a geometric obstruction construction: three point families with alternating coordinate orders realize two incompatible systems of exact-size rectangle constraints. Both branches must use actual captured m-edges despite the absence of a lower horizontal boundary. The full construction and its isolation arguments, rather than only the last counting line, are the counted obligation.

compared.difference: The new finite planar bottomless-rectangle obstruction uses coordinate-separated exact-size trace gadgets, not the infinite progression coloring.

The other selected candidate concerns axis-aligned strips with two-shallow obstruction and a different eleven-group construction. The bottomless three-shallow result is not an immediate change of name or corollary of the strip claim.

editorial_notes: The counted hyperedges are captured m-point traces of bottomless rectangles, as defined at182-183 and used at470/474; source466 contained means captured in this range-family sense, not every subset of a larger trace.

The word northwest for B_i at464 conflicts with the same paragraph precise inequalities x3<x1<x2 and with the native figure. Those explicit coordinates place B_i to the right of A_i and C_i to the left. The author text and figure are retained.
The groups C_i,j lie above b_i^j and below b_i^(j+1) when j<m; for j=m the precise condition y(b_i^k)<y(C_i,j) iff j>=k puts the final group above all B-points. No nonexistent b_i^(m+1) is needed.

The finite copies above the base points can be horizontally scaled into disjoint small neighborhoods, with every non-anchor point above the base line. This realizes the author separate copies without allowing a witnessing rectangle to capture points of another gadget.
In Case2, the m-3 rightmost A-points exclude the leftmost anchor p_i. The four disjoint consecutive triples in B_i use the first12 B-points when m>12.

editorial_scope: One lower-bound construction for shallow hitting sets in a uniform planar range hypergraph. The native figure is part of the proof. Arithmetic progression colorings, strip hypergraphs, and polychromatic upper bounds are not counted.

source_authorship.known_AI_disclosure: No AI-assistance declaration located in read author/abstract/acknowledgement and selected proof; no assertion about undisclosed tools.

review_checkpoints: Explicit x-order is C_i,j left of A_i left of B_i; A lies below every B/C point, while B ascends to the left and each C group ascends to the right.

To select only b_i^j and c_i,j^l with all A: put the right boundary just beyond b_i^j, top just above c_i,j^l, and left boundary just before c_i,j^l; earlier C-points and lower-index B-points are excluded horizontally, later ones vertically.
Every B_i and C_i,j is an m-point edge isolated by suitable horizontal bounds; the global base P is captured below all other points.
For the triple edge choose the left boundary just to the right of p_i, and upper/right boundaries isolating three consecutive B-points. It contains exactly m-3+3 points.

issues_for_independent_review.detail: Check the visible northwest versus explicit x-order clarification and the final C_i,m vertical range. Original source coordinates/figure are supplied; do not invent a different gadget.
Confirm finite separated scaled copies of the supplied coordinate gadget realize all witnessing rectangles and no unintended points.
Assess the entire geometric realization and two-case obstruction, not merely the final triple counting.
